texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.27,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. Due to the impact, the rider and pillion rider fell down on the road. The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and pillion rider died on the way to hospital. The Hebbagodi Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Bolero Pick-Up vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(C) of M.V. Act. It has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner. Further, it has contended that, the alleged accident has taken place due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle and deceased pillion rider, as they were proceeding without helmet and driving licence on a motorcycle Surendhar.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/ 2 bearing No. TN- 70-AH-5617 near Bommasandra-Chandapura service road, in a rash and negligent manner, unmindful of the traffic, resulting in the accident.

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No. KA-01-AL-1236 and

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Safety Engineer at Syngene International Ltd., Biocon Park, Bommasandra Industrial Area and was getting salary of Rs.43,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same he has produced copy of appointment letter, pay slips (6 in nos.) and bank statement as per Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.15.
From these documents it is clear that the petitioner was working as Associate Executive- Production at Syngene International Limited and drawing salary of Rs.43,000/- per month.
b) The petitioner has clearly stated in his cross- examination that, his monthly salary is around Rs.43,000/- and now he is drawing salary of Rs.45,000/- per month.

Further, he has admitted that,
he has received the salary for the period in which he remained absent for his works.
He has applied for the medical leave for the said period and the company has granted medical leave along with salary to him.
Now he is working in the same company in the same cadre.

This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner is continued in the same job and he is doing same work as he was doing before the date of accident and the disability suffered by him is not affecting his work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by him does not arise at all.
For the disability suffered by him, the petitioner may get compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due to disability.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., right leg both bone fracture, right hip posterior dislocated with femur head fracture, abrasion over right cheek, punctured wound over left knee, abrasion over right k

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 08 days from 18-03-2023 to 25-03-2023, in NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center,
Bengaluru.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 8 = Rs.8,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.

As the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 08 days from 18-03-2023 to 25-03-2023, in NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bengaluru, he might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.

Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 8 days as inpatient at NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner admitted during his cross-examination that, he has received the salary for the period in which he remained absent for his works.
He has applied for the medical leave for the said period and the company granted medical leave with salary to him.
Hence, granting compensation for loss of income during the treatment period does not arise in the instant case.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
But, the petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the medical insurance provided by the company will be applicable for future treatments also.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,57,882/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AL-1236 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,57,882/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
